trajectory_summary: The call built real momentum — a cooperative, detail-rich customer moved efficiently through verify with a competent, protocol-aware rep — but it collapsed at the finish when a DQ (utility company not accepting solar applications) surfaced four minutes in, after all the qualifying work was already done. The rep handled the DQ transparently and promised a callback, but the call ends with no appointment and an unresolved thread.
outcome_dispute: This is not a clean DQ in the schema sense of ending pursuit on a hard gate the rep controls — the rep is uncertain ('I'll have to just check with my design team... this looks like it was updated as of a year ago') and promises a callback rather than closing the door. It functions as a callback outcome, not a decisive DQ.

observed_outcome.reasoning: No appointment was set; rep explicitly commits to calling back after checking utility eligibility, but no specific day/time was given, making it an open-ended callback rather than booked/tentative.
